chunks: And from him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from al-Fadl ibn 'Abd al-Malik, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who inherited her husband and then freed him (from slavery); are they upon their first marriage? He said, 'No, but they must renew their marriage.'

key_terms.وَرِثَتْ: inherited (specifically in the context of a free woman marrying a slave, where her dowry/mahr is considered part of the estate or she 'inherits' his status/value in this legal context)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the marriage contract when a free woman's slave husband is freed?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *ikhtilaf al-hurriyyah* (difference in freedom status), establishing that a marriage between a free woman and a slave is valid but becomes suspended or requires renewal upon the slave's manumission. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that the original contract does not automatically persist, necessitating a new *ijad al-nikah* to formalize the union between two free persons. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic principle that the change in the fundamental status of one spouse alters the legal continuity of the marital bond.
